description: Process a raw dual-flow-cell SPR multi-cycle kinetics campaign and recover each analyte's interaction class, rate-resolution status and intrinsic binding constants.
Recover intrinsic rate constants from single-cycle kinetic titrations on a capture surface whose captured ligand level varies and decays.
Choose the interaction model (1:1, bivalent analyte, heterogeneous ligand) for antibody-format SPR data and recover intrinsic site affinities.
Determine solution-phase affinities of tight binders from an SPR inhibition-in-solution assay with a nonlinear calibration and ligand depletion.
Triage a single-concentration SPR fragment screen into specific hits, non-hits and promiscuous compounds from raw dual-surface data.
Recover kinetic constants from a long randomized SPR run in which the ligand surface loses activity, using interleaved positive-control cycles.
Use contact-time-dependent dissociation to identify two-state (induced-fit) versus 1:1 and heterogeneous binding and recover overall affinities.
Derive equilibrium and transition-state thermodynamics, including heat-capacity change, from SPR kinetics recorded at several temperatures.
Assign antibodies to epitope bins from raw SPR tandem (sandwich) binning sensorgrams with dissociation, capture and nonspecific artifacts.
Determine active analyte concentrations by calibration-free concentration analysis from transport-limited SPR binding at two flow rates.
